Hi John / Marissa —

Thanks for the questions — quick answers and a proposed technical eval checklist we usually follow. I attached a short spec (tech-eval-specs.pdf) with test cases. Key points:

- Latency: we split metrics into cold vs warm. For chat workloads we aim for: warm P95 < 200–250ms on a single reasonable GPU configuration (quantized 16–32k context depends). Cold P95 can be higher; we'll measure both.
- Cost: rough order of magnitude (depends on batching/quantization): small-family models (~7–13B) can be in the $0.05–0.15 / 1k token range in optimized runs; 30–70B-class models typically $0.15–0.50 / 1k tokens. We will quantify once you share dataset token distribution.
- Model shortlist (initial, subject to perf):
  * Mistral-Instruct-7B (efficient baseline)
  * Llama-3-70B-q4 (high-quality, quantized)
  * Red-Verified-13B-quant (example Redwood-verified 13B variant)

- Success criteria (proposed):
  1) Functional: >= 90% pass rate on 200 curated prompts for correctness/intent (ACME to define pass/fail rules)
  2) Latency: warm P95 below 250ms for target model on Redwood Dedicated profile Y (we will baseline)
  3) Cost: per-1k-token below agreed threshold (ACME target: <$0.20/1k tokens)
  4) Safety/accuracy checks: no high severity hallucinations in sample set; prompt injection tests pass

- Dependencies: sample dataset (ACME to provide redacted subset), access to evaluation account/keys, preferred instance profile.

Action items for this milestone:
1) ACME: share sample dataset -> due 11/04
2) Redwood (Rishi): deliver test harness + baseline script -> due 11/15
3) Joint: run 2-week benchmark window -> target 11/16–11/30

Attachment: tech-eval-specs.pdf (PDF) — includes test runner instructions and metric dashboard examples.

Happy to jump on 11/9 with Amy and your eng lead to align the dataset and telemetry.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
